subject: Dedicated capacity options for Citrine Labs — proposal and ramp roadmap
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Sep 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Citrine dedicated capacity options

Team —

Putting together the dedicated proposal for Citrine Labs (product search + summarization workloads, long context up to 64k tokens). Quick background: they expect ~250 qps peak for production search reranks, with heavy long-context summarization spikes during nightly batch jobs. They want predictable tail latency and a straightforward ramp.

Draft options I'm thinking to include in the outbound:

- Option A — Small guaranteed pool (entry): 12xA100(80GB) equivalent GPUs reserved, min 12 GPUs available. Auto-burst up to 24 for 30s buckets. Goal: low-cost entry, good for initial production traffic.
- Option B — Production steady: 24xA100-equivalent dedicated GPUs, min guarantee 24, auto-burst to 48. Recommended for customers expecting consistent 200–300 qps.
- Option C — High-throughput ramp: 48xGPU starting commit, staged ramp 24 -> 48 -> 96 over 90 days tied to usage milestones. Includes priority placement and custom cache pre-warming.

Key asks for procurement: preferred term (6/12/24 months), whether they want a 30-day eval credit, and target start date.

Questions for Rishi/Priyom: please sanity-check the min GPU guarantees and a realistic ramp schedule (months and gating metrics). I'd like numbers we can defend with SLA and burst policy descriptions.

Thanks —
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: Citrine dedicated capacity options

Jasmine —

These look solid. A few recommendations based on their described workload:

- Min guarantees should reflect their latency SLOs. For 250 qps and long-context strides: 24 guaranteed is safer as the 'production steady' baseline. 12 could work if we pair with a strong burst and KV-prefix caching to reduce tokens served.
- Ramp cadence: propose a 30-day evaluation (credit covering 50% of usage up to 12 GPUs) -> Month 1: 12 guaranteed / burst to 24 -> Month 2: move to 24 guaranteed / burst to 48 contingent on throughput metrics (95th latency < 300ms) -> Month 3: scale to 48 guaranteed if traffic growth >35% QoQ or sustained p95 < 250ms.
- If they use quantized model variants for batching, call out a discounted CPU-less quantized tier — it materially lowers cost but slightly increases latency variance.
- Include an 'emergency scale' clause: during the first 90 days we allow one-time rapid burst to 96 GPUs for 24 hours as a paid exception.

I'll draft the SLA paragraphs and the cost delta table. Priyom — can you update cost_model_v3 with the 30/60/90-day ramp rows?

-Rishi
Head of Product, Serving Runtime
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@citrinelabs.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel@citrinelabs.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity options for Citrine Labs — proposal

Hi Daniel —

Great speaking earlier in the week. Attached are three dedicated reservation options tailored to Citrine's mixed qps + nightly long-context jobs. Attachments: Citrine_Dedicated_Options_Q3_2025.pdf (proposal decks + option tables) and cost_model_v3.xlsx (detailed monthly burn estimates).

Short summary of options (high level):

- Starter (12 GPU guarantee): Fast time-to-prod, lower monthly commitment, ideal for initial rollout. Includes 30-day evaluation credit (50% credit up to 12 GPUs) and auto-burst to 24 GPUs for short windows.
- Production (24 GPU guarantee): Target for sustained 200–300 qps. Includes priority scheduling, prefix KV caching, and a 2-week warm-up window.
- Growth (48 GPU staged commit): Staged ramp with milestone-based increases and priority placement for pre-warm cache. Recommended if you plan to increase model throughput and long-context usage rapidly.

Questions for you: preferred term length (6/12/24 months), whether procurement wants us to include a 30-day evaluation addendum, and what date you'd like service to start (we can target Oct 6th as a baseline).

Next steps: if this looks good I can drop an updated cost table and a short trial addendum for procurement.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0143
From: Daniel Park <daniel@citrinelabs.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Procurement <sarah.procure@citrine.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options for Citrine Labs — proposal

Jasmine —

Thanks for the clear options. A few quick clarifications from procurement and engineering:

- Procurement (cc'd): we prefer an initial 30-day evaluation with a credit; would like the trial terms addendum.
- On guarantees: engineering is pushing back on starting at 24 guaranteed — they want to prove production traffic consistent before committing. Can we do a 30-day proof-of-concept at 12 guaranteed, then move to 24 if p95 latency and throughput gates are met?
- Also need clearer language on what 'auto-burst' means (taxi bursts vs. sustained bursts) and how overage billing is calculated.

If you can send a short note with the trial addendum and a recommended 30/60/90-day ramp (with gating metrics) that would help speed procurement.

Daniel Park
Head of ML Engineering, Citrine Labs
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@citrinelabs.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options for Citrine Labs — proposal and ramp roadmap

Daniel / team —

Thanks for the feedback — we can absolutely accommodate a 30-day PoC that starts at 12 guaranteed GPUs with a predefined gating plan to move to 24. Outline below (we'll include this in the trial addendum and cost model):

PoC plan (30 days)
- Guarantee: 12 GPUs reserved, ability to auto-burst to 24 for short windows (<= 60s per minute, capped at 10 hours total).
- Credit: Redwood provides a 50% usage credit during PoC (applied to the first invoice).
- Gates at Day 28: move to 24 guaranteed if all of the following met for a rolling 7-day window:
  - sustained throughput >= 180 qps
  - 95th percentile latency (inference) < 300ms
  - error rate < 0.5%
\Month-by-month ramp (if gates met)
- Month 1 (post-PoC): 24 guaranteed, burst to 48 for short windows, regular cache warming.
- Month 2: increase to 36 guaranteed if traffic growth >30% QoQ or p95 < 250ms.
- Month 3: move to 48 guaranteed if usage trends continue.
\SLA / burst billing notes:
- Auto-burst is charged at on-demand hourly rates for the burst duration beyond guaranteed commitment; we log bursts and provide token-level cost breakdowns. Short taxi bursts (<=60s) are not billed beyond a nominal metering fee, but sustained bursts are billed at standard on-demand rates.
\Next steps: I attached updated cost_model_v3.xlsx and a short trial_terms_addendum.pdf. Jasmine — can you send the DocuSign link and an updated proposal PDF with the PoC language? Procurement (Sarah), please send any required legal contacts and preferred PO flow; we'll prepare a DocuSign for signatures once terms are agreed.

Best —
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
